faq.title: Frequently Asked Questions
faq.subtitle: Find answers to common questions about our services and settling in the Netherlands.
faq.question1: How long does the entire settlement process take?
faq.answer1: The timeline varies depending on your specific situation and needs. On average, our clients complete the essential settling steps within 4-8 weeks. Our advisors work to expedite the process wherever possible while ensuring everything is done correctly.
faq.question2: Do I need to speak Dutch to use your services?
faq.answer2: No, all of our services are available in English. Our advisors are bilingual in Dutch and English, and can assist with translation of important documents and communications. We also offer support in several other languages upon request.
faq.question3: What types of housing can you help me find?
faq.answer3: We assist with finding various types of accommodations based on your preferences and budget, including apartments, houses, shared housing, and temporary accommodations. We work with reputable agencies and landlords and can help explain Dutch rental agreements and procedures.
faq.question4: How do your banking services work?
faq.answer4: We have partnerships with several Dutch banks and can facilitate the account opening process. We'll explain the different banking options available, help you prepare the necessary documentation, and in many cases, accompany you to your banking appointment to ensure smooth communication.
faq.question5: What exactly is a postal address?
faq.answer5: A postal address is an address where you receive mail without registering as a resident. Newcomers without a fixed home address use it to apply for a BSN at the municipality.
faq.question6: What does offering a postal address earn me?
faq.answer6: You receive €0.50 to €5 per piece of mail arriving via your address — the more mail, the higher the amount. Helpers also donate €5 per month to support newcomers; you can earn that donation back through the mail compensation.

helpMee.title: Get involved: offer your address as a postal address
helpMee.subtitle: Without a fixed address, a newcomer in the Netherlands cannot apply for a BSN — and without a BSN, no bank account, job or health insurance. You can help by offering your address as a postal address.

what.title: What is a postal address?
what.text: An address where a newcomer's mail is sent. The municipality uses it as a correspondence address so someone without a fixed home address can still apply for a BSN.

not.title: What it is not
not.text: A postal address is NOT a residential registration at your address. Nothing changes about your living situation, rental contract or benefits — it is purely an address for mail.

why.title: Why it helps
why.text: With a BSN a newcomer can open a bank account, work and get insured. Your address is often the first step that sets everything in motion.

steps.title: Helper in three steps
steps.subtitle: From sign-up to first piece of mail — we arrange the match and the handling.

step1.title: Sign up
step1.description: Register as a postal address helper. We verify your details and explain the programme personally.

step2.title: We match you
step2.description: You are matched with one or more newcomers who use your address as a postal address for their BSN application.

step3.title: Receive mail and compensation
step3.description: For every piece of mail arriving via your address you receive €0.50 to €5. The more mail, the higher the amount.

earnings.title: Earn per piece of mail
earnings.subtitle: Compensation starts at €0.50 per piece of mail and rises to €5. You also donate €5 per month to support the programme — a donation you can earn back through the compensation.

start.label: Starting rate
start.text: Per piece of mail received, from the very first one. The baseline to get started.

growth.label: Maximum rate
growth.text: The more mail you receive, the higher the amount per piece — up to a maximum of €5.

donation.label: Monthly donation
donation.text: Every helper contributes €5 per month to support newcomers — so you are partly a donor too.

earnings.note: The maths: you donate €5 per month, but earn it back through the per-mail compensation. At ten pieces of mail a month at €0.50 your donation is already covered — everything above that is net earnings, and you help someone obtain a BSN.
